subtype: Approach: gathering another friend on your side [Action]
passage: Nitin, sit. You say your friends dared you to walk along the compound wall? I will tell you about mine. I am Shalini, and at eleven the boys in my lane dared us all to walk the top of the old wall by the well. My legs felt like water, but everyone was saying yes. Then I noticed Meena at the back, gripping her sleeve, not talking. I edged over and whispered, "You do not want to either, do you?" She shook her head hard. So I said, loud enough, "We are not doing it." Meena said, "Me neither." Two voices, and a boy said, "My mother would kill me anyway." The wall stayed empty, and we told my grandfather about its loose bricks.

qa.q: Who did Shalini notice gripping her sleeve at the back?
qa.a: Shalini noticed Meena gripping her sleeve at the back.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling while everyone said yes to the dare?
qa.a: Frightened, since Shalini's legs felt like water, although nobody had been told.

qa.q: What else could Shalini and Meena do if the boys kept pushing?
qa.a: Walk away together and tell an adult about the wall, because a grown-up can deal with both the dare and the danger.

qa.q: How might Meena feel when Shalini whispered to her?
qa.a: Relieved to find someone who shared her fear, since she shook her head hard and then spoke up. 🙂

grounding: A girl finds another child also uneasy about a dare and says so quietly, and once two say no the group drops it.

subtype: Approach: gathering another friend on your side [Action]
passage: Thunder rumbled over the hills, and Miss D'Souza had said ten minutes, then everyone on the bus. At the old fort wall, Joel's group was daring the girls to climb to the broken turret and touch the flagpole. "Two minutes, easy," he said. "Elizabeth goes first." Elizabeth's hands were cold. The stones were already wet with the first drops. She glanced at Parul, who was twisting her dupatta round and round one finger. "You don't want to either, do you?" Elizabeth whispered. Parul shook her head. Elizabeth took her hand. "We're not climbing," she said out loud. "Me neither," said Parul. There was a pause. Then another girl stepped back too, and Joel shrugged. "Fine. It's raining anyway." They ran for the bus.

qa.q: How long had Miss D'Souza given the class before the bus?
qa.a: She had given them ten minutes.

qa.q: What was Elizabeth feeling before she whispered to Parul?
qa.a: She felt nervous and uneasy, with cold hands, and hoped she wasn't the only one who didn't want to climb.

qa.q: Why did saying no together work better than Elizabeth refusing alone?
qa.a: Once two voices said no, the dare lost its pull: another girl stepped back and Joel dropped it.

qa.q: How might Parul feel when Elizabeth takes her hand?
qa.a: Parul likely feels relieved and braver, because someone has noticed the worry she was showing with her dupatta 🤍.

grounding: Shows a girl quietly finding a classmate who also feels uneasy, so that two refusals make the group drop the dare.

subtype: Approach: gathering another friend on your side [Action]
passage: "Whoever touches the tank on top is gang leader," Deepa announced, pointing at the rusty ladder on the half-built block behind the colony in Chennai. It went up five floors with no cage around it. Everyone cheered. Uma looked at the ladder and her stomach flipped. Then she noticed Karthik at the back, tying and untying his shoelace for the third time. She edged over. "That ladder's rotten," she muttered. "I'm not going." He looked up, relieved. "Me neither. I just didn't want to say." "Say it with me, then." They walked up to Deepa together. "We're out. It's not safe." Deepa laughed, but then Sameer said he was out too, and soon the cheering had turned into an argument about cricket teams.

qa.q: How many floors did the ladder go up?
What was Uma feeling when she looked at the ladder?
qa.a: Her stomach flipped, so she felt scared of the climb, and she was relieved to find that Karthik felt the same.

qa.q: What else could Uma do if the group had kept going?
qa.a: She and Karthik could tell a parent or the building watchman straight away, because a rusty ladder with no cage is dangerous for anyone who tries it.

qa.q: Why might Deepa laugh at first but then let the dare go?
qa.a: Deepa may have felt challenged by the refusal, but once Sameer joined in there was nobody left to cheer, so the dare lost its pull.

grounding: Shows a girl finding a classmate who is also uneasy and saying no together until the group drops the dare.
